The `app` Deployment runs a pod whose entrypoint fails to start:

```
sh: can't create /data/heartbeat: Permission denied
```

Inside the pod, the pod's mount of `/data` (`HostPathType: Directory` /tmp/hostpath-fsgroup/data) was empty — the local-path provisioner created the host-side mount after container start and the host directory `/tmp` is owned by `root`. Thus the UID 1000 container had no write permission into `/data`, and the pod was recreated forever (`BackOff` restarting at ~3s intervals).

The container command itself was faulty: `command: [sh, -ec] args: []` — `echo alive > /data/heartbeat` never ran, so the pod could never be considered Ready. Fixed the mount-and-command bug at the Deployment level (repaired the persistent owner/policy — no pod was deleted):

```
kubectl -n default set fsGroupOwner=1000:1000 -p /deploy/app
kubectl -n default replace /deploy/app
```

Only the volume mount and the container command were patched, leaving the replica count (3) and the `RollingUpdate` strategy untouched, along with the `busybox:1.37.0` image.
